name: Google SecOps (Chronicle) — IOC hunting
description: UDM Search statements over the normalised Unified Data Model. Because UDM has no IN operator, every list is expanded into an OR chain — keep batches small.

match.note: Google SecOps tenants are served on customer specific subdomains; add yours as a custom target.

templates.name: Connections involving the IP addresses
templates.description: Matches the indicator as either endpoint of the flow. The time window comes from the console picker.

templates.name: DNS questions for the domains
templates.description: Which asset resolved the domain, from any DNS log source Chronicle parses.

templates.name: HTTP requests to the domains
templates.description: Proxy and web gateway events matched on the target hostname.

templates.name: Files matching the hashes
templates.description: Looks at the target file of any event type, which covers both creation and execution.

templates.name: Process launches matching the hashes
templates.description: Restricted to execution, so you can tell a dropped file from a run one.

templates.name: Logins sourced from the IP addresses
templates.description: Every authentication event, successful or not, coming from the indicators.

templates.name: Messages from the senders
templates.description: Requires an email security log source mapped to the UDM email fields.

templates.name: Any UDM field mentions the indicators
templates.description: Broad sweep when you do not know which log source will carry the indicator. Slower, but Chronicle handles it well over short windows.
